title: Publish record updates with fresh basis and coherent durable outcomes
statement: The system shall publish structurally valid explicit record updates as one coherent durable transaction after checking expected revision, target identities, and declared decision-basis identities under writer exclusion, with contained writes, safe stale retries, and no usable mixed state.

what.problem: Competing writers, stale decisions, or partial publication can lose work or leave a reader with a combination of states that never existed coherently.
what.desired_outcome: Readers observe one coherent recorded state; contention, drift and interruption do not overwrite winning work or conceal missing evidence.

why.rationale: Reliable mechanical publication is necessary even when the stored engineering judgment is incomplete, adverse, or awaiting review.

stakeholders: Engineers and reviewers operating on recorded engineering work
Engineering agents acting on explicit actor decisions
Maintainers and consumers of the published command-line interface

conditions: During initial creation, targeted or advanced record publication, batch publication, repeated submissions, and concurrent supported reads/writes.

contexts: One explicitly selected Change, its referenced artifacts and declared engineering decision basis, under the supported local writer boundary.

how.approach: Check expected state and declared decision basis, validate the complete candidate and coordinate supported writers before coherent durable publication. Preserve existing successful work and expose interruption without inventing decisions; external engineering-file edits remain subject to observed checks rather than a universal atomicity claim.

how_much.scope: Preserves the published local save-safety boundary. CLI writers coordinate; outside edits are protected at observed identity checks only. An exact-target outside edit after the final check can be overwritten; no atomic exclusion of all external writers, platform expansion, or disaster-recovery service is promised.

acceptance_criteria: Every write names its expected revision, target set and identities, and declared decision-basis identities. Observed mismatches produce conflict requiring reread and a new actor decision, with no silent refresh or merge.

Competing supported writers cannot overwrite one another. Supported readers obtain coherent before/after state or an explicit unavailable/busy/recovery outcome, never a usable mixed state; saved means all selected record effects are durably committed.

Every supported path preserves selected project and Change boundaries and unrelated content. Cross-project or cross-Change mutation, unsafe file destinations where applicable, and unexpected overwrite reject before publication; the physical containment mechanism is an architecture responsibility.

A fresh identical candidate returns unchanged only after current preconditions pass. A lost-response retry with the old revision conflicts even if the earlier save succeeded; no retry duplicates entries, increments semantic state, or creates new approval.

Observed decision-basis drift is checked before publication and again before commitment is reported. Before commit it prevents publication or requires supported uncommitted recovery. If detected after commit, report the actual committed outcome and drift for renewed applicability assessment; never roll back acknowledged commitment or conceal the external-edit timing limitation.

A batch publishes its complete validated candidate coherently. Interruption exposes either an established before/committed state or an explicit recovery condition; a record claiming available evidence cannot commit with an incomplete required payload. Record publication does not atomically govern arbitrary engineering-file edits.
constraints: Current allocations and source-observed facets describe v4 SQLite. Source availability does not establish passing execution, project adoption or requirement satisfaction; historical v3 contribution arguments retain their original subjects.
